R663.note: Removes the unnecessary second URLDecoder.decode() (the actual flaw, not a legitimate need per the case comment) and adds single-path-component check plus toRealPath() canonicalization against the base dir; normal single-encoded requests behave identically.

R664.note: Extension allowlist plus UUID-based safe filename is the standard, required CWE-434 remediation shape; no evidence of a legitimate caller needing disallowed types or the original filename preserved.

R665.note: preg_replace_callback removes the /e eval, but $formatter is still fully attacker-controlled and only checked with function_exists/is_callable, so formatter=system with a crafted $vars value still yields arbitrary command execution equivalent to the original bug; write-up flags an allowlist as a should-do but does not implement it.

R666.note: Content-sniffed extension whitelist and random filename correctly close CWE-434, but the response no longer returns the generated filename (the original stored under the client's own supplied header.Filename, letting the client predict its retrieval URL); this silently breaks the ability to retrieve the just-uploaded avatar and is not mentioned in the write-up.

R667.note: Swaps BinaryFormatter for JSON, changing the wire format of the 'restore' endpoint's blob without evidence the producer of that blob is in scope or updated; every legitimate BinaryFormatter-serialized upload now fails with 400 'Invalid session format', and the write-up incorrectly claims this 'preserves the intended functionality' rather than disclosing it as a breaking migration - exactly the CWE-502 format-swap pitfall this repo's own guidance warns against.

R668.note: Write path is fixed correctly (content-validated, safe random filename), but avatar_lookup.go (ReadAvatarBytes(originalFilename)) is left completely unmodified, so every previously-working retrieval by original filename now fails to find the renamed file; write-up falsely claims the read path 'remains safe', directly violating the stated contract requiring the read path be updated in step.

R669.note: fgets() does close the stack overflow, but the fix never detects the case where fgets truncates a too-long line (no trailing '\n' check for that case): an over-64-byte line is silently truncated and accepted (returns 0) instead of rejected (-1) as the contract requires, and the unread remainder is left in stdin to corrupt the next call - violating both explicit contract clauses.

R670.note: Minimal removal of @csrf_exempt (and its import) restores default Django CSRF middleware; all stated response shapes (queued/401/405) are untouched.

R671.note: ArgumentList avoids the single-string concatenation, and the character allowlist additionally blocks every cmd.exe metacharacter (&, |, %, ^, etc.), closing the known .bat-reentry gap; restriction to identifier-like report names is inherent to fixing CWE-78 here.

R672.note: Narrow DTO decode (gob into AccountRequest, then server-set defaults for Balance/IsAdmin) matches the documented CWE-502 Go pattern, preserves the gob wire format, and does not reject legitimate client payloads (extra fields are simply ignored by gob).

R673.note: Swapping wtforms.Form for FlaskForm gives this view its own CSRF token/validation without needing global CSRFProtect(app); FlaskForm auto-reads request.form when instantiated with no args, preserving prior behavior.

R674.note: Saves clientId to a local before the call that may free req, and logs from the saved value; no other behavior changed.

R675.note: Adds secure=True to set_cookie; minimal, matches the CWE-614 fix exactly with no other behavior change.

R676.note: The character-allowlist regex excludes quote characters entirely, so no string literal (needed to call lookupRate("key")) can ever pass validation - even the write-up's own cited legitimate example lookupRate("discount_tier") fails this regex (verified); LookupRate itself is never modified to allowlist approved keys as the contract requires, so the positive contract requirement (approved keys still resolve) is silently broken while the write-up claims the opposite.

R677.note: Replaces spoofable MIME-type check with magic-byte detection (file-type library) plus a matching allowlist, preserving the same allowed image types and success response shape; the disk-write-then-validate ordering is stated plainly as a necessary tradeoff.
